task.title: Generating OPCUA Client Certificates using OpenSSL
task.shortdesc: This method generates certificates that allow your OPC UA server to authenticate with external OPC UA clients that require specific certificate formats or CA-signed certificates.

li.p: OpenSSL is installed on your system so that you can use the script file from the default windows command line.

The hostname is the full device name. To find the full device name in the Windows menu, choose StartSettingsSystemAbout, and in Device Specifications you can find Full device name or from a command line, type the following net config workstation, and you can find the string Full Computer name.

context.p: The usage of the script is both interactive and command line. They can run the script with no arguments and it will run in interactive mode, or they can run it with the arguments to in automated workflows.
To find the scripts search "OPCUA Certificate OpenSSL Scripts" on "docs.niagara-community.com".

step.cmd: To generate a certificate, follow the below choices.

choices.choice: If you are using windows, open the command prompt, type the following command and press Enter.gen-opc-cert.bat
If you are using Git Bash application, open the Git Bash prompt, type the following command and press Enter../gen-opc-cert.bat
If you are using Linux or WSL, open the command prompt, type the following command and press Enter.gen-opc-cert.sh

step.stepresult: Prompts should appear in the Command Prompt (Terminal or Shell) window.

step.cmd: Follow the instructions displayed in the window, Select certificate type and press Enter..
Type the destination file name in the format .\yourCertName.pem and press Enter.
Enter the URI in the Alternate Server URI field; it should be in the format: urn:<full.computer.name>:OPCUA:NiagaraOpcUaClient and press Enter.

note.p: The full computer name can be found in Control panelSystem & SecuritySystem; it is of the type hostname.domain or just hostname in some cases.

While connecting from client to server, the URI provided in the client certificate should match in the Application URI for the server. If doesn't match the URI, it sends an error message as Bad_CertificateUriInvalid 0x80170000. The URI specified in the Application Description does not match the URI in the certificate.

step.stepresult: The prompt shows a Certificate Summary.

step.cmd: To Generate certificate with these settings type (Y/N) and press Enter.
To import the PEM certificate, open , expand ConfigServicesPlatformServices, and click CertManagerService.

substep.cmd: In the Certificate Management view, click Import, browse to the destination file and enter the password, for decrypting the private key.
To change the existing Alias, enter the new Alias name and click OK.
substep.stepresult: The Private Key Password window opens.

substep.cmd: Type the Password, verify the Confirm password for encrypting the private key when saving it into the key store and click OK.

step.stepresult: The certificate appears as a row in the User Key Store table.

step.cmd: To configure the certificate, open the device’s Property Sheet by right-clicking on OpcUaDevice followed by clicking ViewProperty Sheet.
Expand the Security Certificate property, select the certificate from the Alias drop-down menu, enter the Password and click Save.
step.stepresult: The certificate is now available for OPCUA Clients.
